outputs: negotiation dialogues where agents try to reach agreements on dividing items with specific point values

changes_made.explanation: Removed specific model variants (M_p=...) as they are instances of the main models, not different model types. Simplified output descriptions to be more concise. Kept core models only.

Normalized metric names to title case. Removed redundant/overly specific metrics (e.g., 'points scored by human' is covered by 'Points scored'). 'Utility' is the theoretical concept, not an evaluation metric.
No LLMs were used as judges in this paper. The paper does mention future work with LLMs, but not for evaluation.

guideline: Participants negotiated with agents and answered post-survey questions on satisfaction with outcome and likeness toward opponent using 5-point Likert scales

changes_made.explanation: Removed objective metrics (points scored, walkaways) from human evaluation criteria - these are automatic metrics, not subjective human judgments. Kept only the actual subjective criteria asked in the human evaluation survey.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on negotiation dialogue systems evaluation. The extraction was generally good but included some redundancies and confusion between automatic metrics and human evaluation criteria. The core NLG task is dialogue generation, evaluated through both automatic metrics (points-based) and human evaluation (subjective ratings).
